title: What can you say about ginkgo in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 3 wordings for ginkgo; the strongest is "Helps support cognitive function in adults" (moderate, 80-240 mg standardized extract a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Treats dementia or Alzheimer's disease".

supported_wordings.wording: Helps support cognitive function in adults.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it at 80-240 mg of standardized extract a day; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older. Health Canada: 80-240 mg of standardized extract a day (4-12 g dried leaf), at least 80 mg per dose. Ask a health care practitioner for use beyond 8 months (80 to under 120 mg a day), 6 weeks (120-180 mg) or 4 weeks (over 180 mg).
supported_wordings.form: Leaf extract, standardized to 22-27% flavonoid glycosides and 5-7% terpene lactones

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Thins the blood, or works like a blood thinner
wordings_to_avoid.why: Describes a drug action. Health Canada says not to use ginkgo with blood thinners.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
